title: Cohomological boundedness of the localizing exceptional object
statement:
Fix a universe u, a prime $\ell$, and a field $k$ in universe u of positive
characteristic different from $\ell$. Let $Z,Y$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes
and let $g:Z\to Y$ be a proper $k$-morphism [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $\Lambda$ be one of the following three commutative condensed coefficient rings,
with its specified multiplication: $\underline E$ for a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$,
$\underline{\mathcal O_E}$ for its valuation ring, or the finite-subextension-valued
ring $\underline{\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell}$ [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring;
sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed].
For $T=Z,Y$, put $\Lambda_T=p_T^*\Lambda$, let $D_T=D(\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_T})$
be the ordinary unbounded module-object derived category
[sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], let $\mathcal B_T$ be its bounded constructible
full subcategory [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible], and let
$\mathcal L_T=\operatorname{Loc}(\mathcal B_T)$ be the full localizing hull, using
ambient coproducts indexed in universe u+1
[def-sfb-bounded-constructible-localizing-closure].
Let $F_g:\mathcal L_Z\to\mathcal L_Y$ be the canonical restriction of the ambient
$Rg_*$ [lem-sfb-adic-proper-localizing-pushforward]. For every functor $G:\mathcal L_Y\to\mathcal L_Z$, every supplied adjunction $F_g\dashv G$, and every $K\in\mathcal B_Y$, there exist integers $a\le b$ such that $H^i((G(K)).\mathrm{obj})=0$ for all integers $i$ with $i<a$ or $b<i$. Here $K$ is included into $\mathcal L_Y$ by the canonical full inclusion, and the homology is computed in the ordinary ambient module-object derived category. No choice of a right adjoint is part of the assertion.

lean.statement: theorem ellAdic_localizing_rightAdjoint_obj_isBounded (G : (boundedConstructibleLocalizingClosure Λ Y.left).FullSubcategory ⥤ (boundedConstructibleLocalizingClosure Λ Z.left).FullSubcategory) (adj : ellAdicLocalizingLowerStar Λ ℓ g hΛ ⊣ G) (K : (boundedConstructible (condensedRingObj Λ Y.left)).FullSubcategory) : ∃ a b : ℤ, ∀ i : ℤ, (i < a ∨ b < i) → IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ i).obj ((G.obj ((boundedConstructibleToLocalizing Λ Y.left).obj K)).obj))

proof.text: The three coefficient rings are exactly the explicitly listed rings in the statement: the first two are the continuous-function condensed rings for a finite $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ and its valuation ring, and the third is the finite-subextension-valued ring. Both $Z$ and $Y$ are Noetherian: the field $k$ is Noetherian because its only ideals are $0$ and $k$, and apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] to their structure maps. They are qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-over-affine]. Their underlying spaces are topologically Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal]. Every locally closed stratum has Noetherian underlying space as well: an increasing chain of subspace opens can be written as intersections with an increasing chain of ambient opens, by replacing ambient representatives with their successive unions. We will use the coefficient comparisons on these actual strata.

source.place: Tag 01T6, lemma-finite-type-noetherian; coefficient cases of the source restriction proof

proof.text: For $T=Z,Y$ and $\Lambda=\underline E$ or $\underline{\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell}$, compare the two constructibility predicates on a cohomology module $P$. If $P$ is constructible in the general ring-object sense, choose its finite stratification with locally finitely presented restrictions. On each stratum [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-lfp-local-triviality], respectively [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-qbar-lfp-local-triviality], makes the restriction pro-étale locally finite free. A finite free module is the constant scalar model obtained from the finite-dimensional scalar vector space of the same rank, so $P$ has the finite constant local models of [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. Conversely a finite constant local model is locally finitely presented by [det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model]. Thus the predicates agree. The algebraic-closure case uses precisely the finite-subextension-valued ring specified in the statement; it does not replace that ring by all norm-continuous functions.

source.place: Example 3.1 and Theorem 6.2: scalar local models; coefficient-specific lfp bridges are the cited separate obligations

proof.text: For $\Lambda=\underline{\mathcal O_E}$ and $T=Z,Y$, apply both implications of [lem-sfb-integral-lfp-constant-model-comparison] to every module $P$ on $T$. The hypotheses are satisfied by the Noetherian schemes in step 1 and by the continuous integral condensed coefficient ring. Its conditions (i) and (ii) are exactly the general ring-object constructibility predicate and the scalar finite-constant-model predicate used here. Torsion is allowed, so this argument does not assert local freeness for an arbitrary integral constructible module. Consequently the same equality of constructibility predicates holds for integral coefficients.

source.place: Definition 6.8.10 and Proposition 6.8.11(3); the cited coefficient comparison supplies the general-lfp bridge

proof.text: Apply the predicate equalities in steps 2 and 3 to each cohomology module of an arbitrary ambient complex on $T=Z,Y$. Boundedness is the same finite-interval vanishing condition in [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible] and [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. Hence $\mathcal B_T=\mathcal D^b_c(T,\Lambda)$ as full subcategories of the same ordinary unbounded module-object derived category. Clause (2) of [det-def-localizing-closure-ctf-equals-bc] gives $\mathcal D^b_c=\mathcal D^b_{ctf}$. The localizing hulls also agree: the defining intersections in [def-sfb-bounded-constructible-localizing-closure] and [sk-def-localizing-closure] now range over the identical replete triangulated properties containing the identical generators and closed under the identical ambient coproducts. Take their fixed indexing universe to be u+1 throughout. In particular the object $K$ in the question is an object of $\mathcal D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$, and its inclusions into the two descriptions of the hull agree.

source.place: Clause (2), followed by the intersection definitions of the two hulls

proof.text: Let $R=Rg_!$ on the localizing categories and let $H=g^!$ be the right adjoint supplied by [sk-prop-sf-existence]. These categories are the ones identified in step 4. Since $g$ is proper, clause (1) of [det-cor-existence-ii-restriction] gives a natural isomorphism $\alpha:R\xrightarrow{\sim}F_g$, where $F_g$ is the canonical ambient-pushforward restriction of [lem-sfb-adic-proper-localizing-pushforward]. Only clause (1) is used, not that node's constructibility conclusion. For rational coefficients [sk-thm-restriction] gives $H(K)\in\mathcal D^b_{ctf}(Z,\Lambda)$. For integral coefficients [det-prop-int-brown-adjoint] identifies its integral adjoint with this same $H$ under the equalities of step 4, and [sk-thm-int-restriction] gives $H(K)\in\mathcal D^b_{ctf}(Z,\mathcal O_E)$. The hypothesis on $g$ needed by these restriction theorems is separated finite type, which follows directly from properness. This establishes boundedness for $H(K)$ in every coefficient case before making any claim about $G(K)$.

source.place: The rational and integral bullets; proper comparison is clause (1) of det-cor-existence-ii-restriction

proof.text: Transport the supplied adjunction $F_g\dashv G$ across $\alpha$. Explicitly, its Hom bijection for $A\in\mathcal L_Z$, $B\in\mathcal L_Y$ is composed with $\operatorname{Hom}(RA,B)\to\operatorname{Hom}(F_gA,B)$, $t\mapsto t\circ\alpha_A^{-1}$. This is natural and bijective, with inverse given by composition with $\alpha_A$, so it is an adjunction $R\dashv G$. Now $G$ and $H$ are right adjoints of the same functor on the entire localizing categories. Apply [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint] to obtain a natural isomorphism $G\simeq H$. In particular its component at the included $K$, followed by the full-subcategory inclusion into the ambient derived category on $Z$, gives an isomorphism of the underlying objects $G(K)\simeq H(K)$. No adjunction restricted merely to constructible test objects is used in this comparison.

source.place: Transpose and mutually inverse comparison for two right adjoints

proof.text: By step 5, $H(K)$ belongs to $\mathcal D^b_{ctf}$, which by [sk-def-sfb-constructible] is a full subcategory of bounded complexes with constructible cohomology. Choose bounds $a\le b$ for its cohomology. For each integer $i$, apply the ambient homology functor in degree $i$ to the isomorphism of step 6. Its image is an isomorphism $H^i(G(K))\simeq H^i(H(K))$ because a functor takes inverse morphisms to inverse morphisms. The right-hand object is zero for $i<a$ or $b<i$, and composing that isomorphism with its zero-object structure proves the same vanishing for the left-hand object. These bounds therefore answer the question for the originally supplied $G$ and adjunction. If $Z$ is empty or $K$ is zero the same argument applies, and bounds $a=b=0$ may be used for a zero image.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-N6-a2b0bfa17 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole item, the parent, the ancestor, the unit record and every cited statement, plus det-existence-restriction.proof.md, Stacks 01T6, Bhatt–Scholze Def 6.8.10 and Prop 6.8.11, Mathlib Adjunction/Unique.lean:102-133, and the live Lean IsEllAdicCoefficient and padicAlgClRingObj (EllAdic.lean:161-235). Statement: positive characteristic is now explicit, matching the parent, the setting and the Lean Fact (ringChar k).Prime. The three coefficient rings are listed directly; they are exactly the three constructors of the Lean certificate, and the Qbar ring is the finite-subextension ring. The worker's counterexample showing it differs from all continuous maps is correct. Nothing is weakened. Proof steps: (1) Z and Y are Noetherian and qcqs, and the subspace-Noetherian argument holds. (2) and (3) show the general-lfp and constant-model constructibility predicates agree, through the E/Qbar lfp bridges on Noetherian strata and the integral comparison, which allows torsion. (4) B_T equals Dbc equals Dctf in D(Mod_{Λ_T}) by ctf-equals-bc clause (2); the two hulls are the same intersection, with the universe u+1 consistent with def-weil-size-convention. (5) H = g^! of sk-prop-sf-existence; clause (1) of det-cor-existence-ii gives Rg_! ≅ F_g; sk-thm-restriction and int-brown-adjoint plus sk-thm-int-restriction give H(K) in Dctf. This is the blueprint route. (6) The supplied adjunction is transported along α and rightAdjointUniq gives G ≅ H on the whole hull. (7) The vanishing bounds transfer across that isomorphism. Edge cases K=0, Z empty, g=id and torsion O_E/ℓ are fine. No new nodes; proof_deps equals the union of the uses; no SGA. Accepted tool_uses: the two lfp bridges, the integral comparison and ctf-equals-bc; the pbc scheme lemmas are Mathlib leaves. For maintenance: the wording of (iii) in def-sfb-adic-coefficient-certificate, 'C(-,Qbar)', should read the finite-subextension ring, as in its citation and the Lean.
